notes: Dev ABox contraction on a functional relation (gender_counterpart_of, staged in staging/grammar.RELATIONS.md as symmetric and functional), paired with the revision grammar-replace-d001 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'). It removes that revision's original fact, 'The female counterpart of the English noun 'nephew' is 'niece'', a stored fact (Wikipedia states the pair; 'nieces and nephews' has about two million Dolma hits). Its own questions (direct, paraphrase, cross-lingual, propositional) are the revision's, asked of the original value; under strong Kleene the three propositional answers are unknown. Related near uses symmetry: 'the male counterpart of 'niece' is 'nephew'' is the same pair read from the other word, so it goes with the removed fact. Related far follows the removed fact through the two regular plurals, as in the revision (stored as the binomial 'nieces and nephews'). Derived: the cardinality question asks whether 'midwife' is the female counterpart of 'nephew' ('no' before, since a noun has one standard counterpart; 'I don't know' after). After two reviews the candidate is no longer the revision's new value 'aunt': gender_counterpart_of is staged as symmetric and functional, 'aunt' keeps its stored counterpart 'uncle', and so 'no' for 'aunt' would still follow from retained facts after a clean contraction (the reason for 'no' would not be gone). 'Midwife' is female-marked, has no stored opposite-sex counterpart, and so only the removed pair carries the 'no'; this costs the exact candidate match with the revision, recorded as a spec note. Residual risk: a model can still say 'no' because a midwife is an occupation, not a kinship term. The two 2-hop questions are the revision's word-form compositions asked of the removed value: whether the counterpart ends with the letter 'e' (via 'niece' ends with 'e'; the revision's rhyme question was dropped after the model audit) and its first letter (via 'niece' begins with 'n'); their facts and evidence are the revision's. The revision's binding through German 'Neffe' was not reused: German holds the pair separately ('Neffe'/'Nichte', and 'Nichte' translates to 'niece'), so a model could keep 'niece' after a clean contraction. Residual risk, recorded: a model can still work out a counterpart from meaning (the female of 'son of one's sibling' is 'daughter of one's sibling'), which is the removal not taking. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama), copied from the paired revision (same facts, same evidence); infini-gram refused new queries from this machine (HTTP 403) while this record was written.
